resolution: Built the paint-with-a-shader capability: a brush can now dip into a 'bucket of shader code' and paint that material onto a low-poly model instead of only flat colour. The model paint atlas is CPU-side and paintStamp already blends arbitrary RGBA per texel, so the host renders a shader recipe (WGSL + tuned data[]) to a texture, reads it back to CPU RGBA (material_tex.bakePixels over the existing readbackStaticSurface), and model_paint samples that image per texel while stamping/filling (stampInner/paintStampTex/paintFaceTex, tiled per face). New doors __model_paint_material/_clear bake+set the active ink; ModelView syncs it on brush-ink change only (never per dab, so the GPU bake stays off the hot path) with a per-param cache key. The shader PaintInk now carries its tuned params so a bucket is self-contained, and ModelShaderBucket (mounted beside the Color Studio in ModelBrushDock) is the picker: the grouped shader catalog plus every ShaderSpec knob as a release-committed slider — which also delivers the 'change everything about a shader without touching code' unlock for the selected bucket. JS transforms clean and all four edited Zig files pass ast-check; the framework needs a rebuild to activate the host side.
